- [TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/04/08 (Sat) 11:46
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] CHAPTER EIGHTEEN: Special Conditions
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The author provides guidance for individuals who suffer from more extreme or special conditions causing back pain.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Seeking medical help is necessary for these conditions.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The book's concepts and exercises can provide a great foundation for building a more specific treatment plan.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The chapter begins by discussing disc herniations, a severe condition that requires medical attention.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] If the pain is too severe to start with the book, a steroid injection may be necessary to calm the pain down.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Nerve flossing is recommended to remove disc material or scar tissue that can cause or exacerbate pain.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The author addresses hypermobile sacroiliac (SI) joint pain, which can be one of the most challenging and stubborn conditions to treat.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] In addition to medical intervention, isometric adduction and abduction exercises are recommended to strengthen the muscles without moving the unstable SI joint.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The author concludes by reminding readers to strike a balance between medical help and the advice provided in the book.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] A two-sided approach can provide significant relief for individuals with these special conditions.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Seeking specific treatment after building a foundation with the book's exercises can lead to a complete, permanent solution.
